---
title: "Analyse a position"
subtitle: "Ranked moves, equity, and the win/gammon/backgammon split"
---

::: {.lead}
Same engine as the [playable board](play.qmd), same rough edges — here you move
both sides, so you can set up a position and ask what the network makes of it.
:::

::: {.raccoon-app data-mode="analyse" data-size="full"}
:::

::: {.app-fallback}
The analyser needs JavaScript and WebAssembly. The same engine runs
[in a terminal](how.qmd).
:::

**Bring a position.** Paste an XGID from XG, GNU Backgammon or Backgammon Galaxy
and the board will load it; edit the board by hand if you prefer; copy the XGID
back out when you are done. **Analyse** ranks every legal play for the dice on
screen.

**What the numbers mean.** Every legal play is ranked by cubeless equity in
points, from the perspective of the player on roll, together with the
probabilities of winning plain, with a gammon, and with a backgammon — read
straight from the network's six-outcome value head. Equity differences are shown
against the best play, which is the same quantity the
[strength measurements](strength.qmd) are built from.

**Cube decisions are not analysed.** The cube fields of an XGID are read and
displayed but not evaluated: this engine is cubeless for now, and a cube model is
[milestone 3](roadmap.qmd).
